common_weak_responses: Unit errors going unnoticed
dangerous_misconceptions: Keep all framing non-clinical or clinically trivial. Never require drug-dosing knowledge.

topic: Reading a chart or table accurately
must_understand: Axes, units, scale, time period, and what is actually plotted.
assessment: Data interpretation station.
common_weak_responses: Describing the shape without reading the axes | Extrapolating beyond the data
dangerous_misconceptions: QUB states explicitly there are no data or graph stations; Manchester has no reading at all. Serve data stations only where the school profile supports them.

topic: Stating what the data cannot show
must_understand: That the highest-value response names the limits — no comparator, no denominator, truncated axis, aggregation hiding variation.
assessment: Data interpretation with MISLEAD set high.
common_weak_responses: Answering only what was asked | Accepting the presentation uncritically
dangerous_misconceptions: This is the discriminating behaviour and should be weighted above arithmetic accuracy.

topic: AI in healthcare — what it does
must_understand: That AI in the NHS is currently strongest in triage, documentation and image analysis rather than autonomous diagnosis. As at 2026: NHS England announced an AI acceleration on 4 July 2026 within a £10bn three-year technology programme — AI triage in the NHS App, ambient voice documentation in outpatients, Copilot for 500,000+ staff.
assessment: Policy discussion.
common_weak_responses: 'AI will replace doctors' or 'AI will never replace doctors' with no mechanism | Discussing AI in general rather than in a named use case
dangerous_misconceptions: FAST. The tester named this as a gap. Review quarterly.

must_understand: That the GMC's position is that accountability does NOT transfer — practitioners remain responsible for decisions taken using new technologies, must discuss their use with patients including uncertainties and limitations, must work within their competence, and must report adverse incidents involving software and digital tools. On 29 July 2026 the MHRA clarified that transcription, summarisation and letter drafting are not medical devices, while ambient voice technology that supports diagnosis or acts without clinician review IS a regulated medical device.
assessment: Policy discussion with hostile follow-up: 'If the AI was wrong, who is responsible?'
common_weak_responses: Not addressing accountability at all | Assuming the manufacturer bears clinical responsibility
dangerous_misconceptions: This is the single best-differentiated AI sub-question and almost nobody teaches it. The regulatory boundary is unstable — a functionality change can silently alter a product's regulatory status.

must_understand: That training-data bias can widen inequity, that automation bias makes clinicians over-trust outputs, and that deskilling is a live concern as documentation and triage become default.
assessment: Policy discussion.
common_weak_responses: Naming 'bias' with no mechanism or example
dangerous_misconceptions: A candidate who can name a mechanism — under-representation in training data leading to worse performance in a subgroup — substantially outperforms one who names the word.

topic: Health data, consent and public trust
must_understand: The tension between data-driven care and consent at scale; the Single Patient Record confirmed in the King's Speech on 13 May 2026 within the NHS Modernisation Bill; the Federated Data Platform controversy, including reporting in May 2026 that NHS England planned to grant Palantir and external consultancy staff admin-level access to identifiable patient data, with an internal briefing acknowledging risk of loss of public confidence.
assessment: Policy discussion.
common_weak_responses: Treating data sharing as either obviously good or obviously sinister
dangerous_misconceptions: FAST and contested. Present both the care-improvement case and the trust case; never signal a position.

must_understand: That making the NHS App the front door disadvantages people without smartphones, connectivity, digital skills or English — disproportionately older, poorer and disabled people, who use care most. This is the inverse care law restated for the digital era.
assessment: Policy discussion.
common_weak_responses: Discussing digital transformation with no equity dimension
dangerous_misconceptions: A high-value link between two topics most candidates treat separately. Reward the connection.

must_understand: That genomic medicine is moving from diagnosis of rare disease toward population stratification — newborn genomic screening, targeted screening by genetic risk — and that this creates consent, incidental-finding, insurance and equity problems.
assessment: Policy discussion.
common_weak_responses: Enthusiasm with no downside | Confusing genomic screening with genetic engineering
dangerous_misconceptions: Newborn genomic screening raises consent for someone who cannot consent, and a finding that cannot be un-known. That tension is the assessable content.
